correctness.rationale: For \(nT^2\le1\) the radial symbol is positive semidefinite and the Schur multiplier is completely positive of norm one. For \(nT^2>1\) the explicit \(H\pm M\) Gram kernels and matching weighted trace-norm witness analytically establish both ordinary and completely bounded norms exactly, including \(n=1\). Bounded diagonal kernel factorizations plus finite-corner exhaustion give the infinite-star law. Rational checks on 10,559 cases supplement but do not replace the universal proof; all normalizations and boundary parameters have been reconstructed.
